thread:
Alex R: FYI — hiring manager flagged an exception. Maia (SWE IC3) offer needs an out-of-cycle comp uplift + a 'parachute' clause that allows start to slip up to 60 days with a prorated sign-on if visa/delays occur. Can we route approval and confirm benefits eligibility window?
Marisa G: Can you paste the proposed comp and sign-on numbers? Also need the business justification paragraph for the packet.
Alex R: Comp: $215,000 base + $35k sign-on (split: $20k immediate, $15k conditional on 6mo). Reason: high local market + counteroffer risk. Hiring mgr says immediate start target May 15 but visa might push to July.
Jonah K: Got it. That base is IC4 band floor at our bands table. Did you get manager approval for band exception? If not, you'll need director sign-off.
Alex R: Manager (Erin L) verbally approved band uplift, but we need written routing. Erin — can you confirm in thread?
Erin L: Confirmed — I approve IC4 uplift for Maia. This is a critical hire for infra team; remote in EU with relocation stipend. Happy to sign the doc.
Liz P: HR note: benefits eligibility will start on employee's official start date. If we allow a delayed start with parachute clause, we need to decide whether sign-on pro-rate triggers at new start or original offer date. Typically we tie to actual start.
Marisa G: For approvals: route to Comp Committee -> Legal for parachute language -> Finance for sign-on schedule. I can kick off comp committee note today if Alex drops justification + org impact bullet.
Alex R: Pasting justification snippet I used: "Candidate has live counteroffer. Market comparators show 10-15% premium for similar roles in EU region. Candidate requires relocation and has critical infra skills (serving runtime ops). Risk of losing candidate delays roadmap." Happy to edit.
HR Bot: Comp Committee request form: https://redwood.example/comp-requests. Attach: offer packet, manager approval, salary comps. Use request_type=band_exception
Alex R: @Marisa submitted draft to comp request form and attached offer + manager note. Wanted to confirm parachute language: proposed snippet — "If employee's start date is delayed beyond 30 days for visa or relocation reasons, sign-on will be prorated by 50% for delays between 31-60 days; beyond 60 days, company may withdraw the sign-on portion." Thoughts?
Jonah K: Legal needs to review before Finance signs off. Also suggest adding explicit rollback if start >90 days. Otherwise ok as a temporary measure. :eyes: 
Liz P: Agree re: tying benefits to actual start. Also note relocation stipend tax implications — need payroll loop-in.
Marisa G: I'll route right now: comp committee (today), then legal (tomorrow EOD), finance (after legal). If comp committee ok, we can issue conditional offer by EOD. @Erin L please be ready to sign when comp approved.
Erin L: Will sign asap. :thumbsup: 
Alex R: Thanks team — will monitor. Please ping me in thread with any missing docs. Appreciated. :pray:
